text:
marta: quick follow-up on the hybrid-ingress shaper RFC — wanted to capture some tradeoffs we didn't nail in the doc. leaning toward local admission with periodic central reconciliation. thoughts?

liam: +1 for local admit to keep tail latency down. main worry is cross-GPU fairness; local-only can starve tenants on certain shards.

sasha: agree with liam. also worried about abuse signals — central has better global view for scoring. local admit + blind local heuristics = weird edge cases.

anika: idea: local admit for p50/p95, central reconciliation to adjust tokens + slow-path routing for persistent offenders. maintain small lease tokens locally and reconcile every ~1s.

marta: lease tokens + periodic reconciliation seems pragmatic. we need to be explicit about signal TTLs so we don't overreact to short spikes. what TTL are we thinking?

jing: propose 3s ephemeral window for burst allowance, 30s smoothing window for abuse score. abuse score updates from central and edge heuristics (client fingerprint + model mix).

liam: if we do 3s bursts, we should limit embedding-heavy tenants differently — embeddings chew GPU differently vs chat. need per-model weight in the admission calc.

anika: +1. suggest admission weight = tokens * model_cost_factor. weight for embedding v2 = 3x text-gen baseline. that keeps fair shares meaningful.

marta: sketch of local config example (for ops and config owners):
```
ingress:
  local_admit: true
  burst_window_sec: 3
  smoothing_window_sec: 30
  token_bucket:
    capacity: 2000
    refill_per_sec: 400
  model_weight_overrides:
    embedding-v2: 3.0
    chat-medium: 1.0
```

sasha: two more failure modes: 1) central reconciliation lag — local nodes keep admitting bad clients for longer, 2) split-brain when central control plane flaps. need safe fallback.

marta: for (1) we can bound max local burst tokens per client per node so damage window is limited. for (2) fallback = degraded fairness: prefer per-tenant min-reservations and global min-slices. basically conservative defaults.

liam: operationally, how do we route when a tenant exceeds local budget? options: 1) reject, 2) route to cheaper model variant, 3) throttle to best-effort queue. I prefer (2) + (3) depending on tenant tier.

jing: implement as routing policy matrix: {tier: [primary_model, fallback_model, admission_policy]}. quick sample: free -> [gpt-lite, none, reject]; pro -> [gpt-2, gpt-2-quant, queue].

anika: we also need abuse detection signals in telemetry so reviewers can see who is hitting fallbacks. include: fallback_count, avg_fallback_latency, tokens_on_fallback.

marta: rollout plan proposal: dark launch local admit on 10% of nodes with metric gating, then canary 2 clusters, monitor p99 latency, fallback_count, token-leakage, error rate, and model-utilization.

liam: test matrix: synthetic workload mix (spammy small requests, embedding hammer, normal chat), shard hotspotting test, central flapping simulation, and client fingerprint spoofing tests.

ops-bot: deploy checklist created: https://go/internal/runbooks/hybrid-ingress-checklist (draft) :white_check_mark:

marta: action items: 1) anika to write local admit config + admission math (due EOD Thu), 2) jing to add telemetry counters and dashboards (due Mon), 3) liam to own synthetic test harness (due next Wed), 4) sasha to draft safety fallback policy doc (due Fri). I'll coordinate the dark launch.

sasha: small nit — we should consider token vs request quotas. some clients send many tiny requests, others few huge ones. admission should be token-weighted but we need request caps to prevent meta-DoS (control-plane churn).

anika: agreed. add separate request_rate limiter with lower granularity and a backoff header so clients can retry sensibly.

marta: last thought: for canary we should enable an automatic rollback if p99 increases > 30% or fallback_count > threshold. infra-bot, can we wire that?

infra-bot: yes — we can add automated rollback hook keyed on metric alarms. will draft runbook snippet and PR.

liam: :thumbsup: ok let's not let perfect be the enemy of good — local admit + central reconciliation + conservative fallbacks seems workable.

marta: thanks all — I'll update the RFC with decisions and link the runbook + sample config. ping me if you want to join the working group.

ops-bot: note: created incident channel #hybrid-ingress-darklaunch for canary ops.

marta: closing thread — will post the updated doc in ~1h. :sparkles:
